title: eludite.debug.start input
description: Debug > Start Debugging (F5) or Start Without Debugging (Ctrl+F5): build the startup project first (when the setting build.beforeRun is on, the default: eludite.build.project's build, streamed to the Output window) and, when the build succeeds, run its built program (`dotnet` on its DLL) with its launchSettings.json profile's arguments and environment, under the netcoredbg debug adapter or, without debugging, with its output in the Output window's Debug source. A failed or canceled build does not launch: the Error List comes forward and the status bar says why. Refused while a session is running or building (use eludite.debug.continue to resume a break).

project.description: The project to run: its path (absolute or relative to the solution folder) or its name as the Workspace window shows it. Default: the startup project (eludite.workspace.set_startup_project), else the solution's first executable project.

debug.description: False runs without the debugger (Ctrl+F5). Default true.

profile.description: The launchSettings.json profile to use. Default: the first profile whose commandName is Project.

build.description: Build the project before launching. Default: the setting build.beforeRun (true unless changed).

wait_ms.description: How long to wait for the debuggee to break, exit or settle before answering, in milliseconds. From the UI the command never waits; from another thread (an agent) the default is 5000. A build before the launch counts against it: an answer with mode `building` or `launching` means the session is still starting; read eludite.debug.state later.
